GENERAL SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Reproduction? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Reproduction.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproduction.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Human Reproduction.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Reproduction.

3. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. A mixture of two liquids

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts ? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Decomposers only

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Sensory and endocrine system in Human Beings ● The structure and functions of se.

8. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

9. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Only water vapour

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating ? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. joule (J)
   C. watt (W)
   D. newton (N)

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain The Mole 2.3 Hydrocarbons 3.0 Natural Physical Science 3.1 Thin Lenses 3.2 Newto and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain The Mole ● Relative Atomic Mass of elements ● Conversions of chemical quantities and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Hydrocarbons ● Classification of hydrocarbons ● General formula and Nomenclature and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
